subject: Security

findings.subject: Security
findings.title: Database credentials modeled as plaintext config fields in version-controlled appsettings files
findings.recommendation: The committed value is currently only a placeholder ("<DevUser password>"), not a live secret, but the Password field is part of the checked-in appsettings.json/appsettings.Development.json schema and is interpolated directly into a plaintext connection string in TestingRepository.BuildConnectionString. This structure invites a developer to paste a real credential straight into a file tracked by git. Remove the Password field (and ideally the whole credential set) from the committed appsettings*.json, and source it exclusively via dotnet user-secrets in Development and environment-variable/Key Vault injection in higher environments (the project already declares a UserSecretsId, so wire that up instead of a config placeholder). Add a pre-commit/CI secret scan to catch accidental real values in these files.

strengths.subject: Security
strengths.title: Global exception middleware returns generic, correlation-ID-based error responses instead of leaking stack traces or internal messages

evidence.excerpt: var loggingCorrelation = LoggingUtilities.GetLoggingCorrelation(); this.logger.LogError(exception, "{UserMessage}", loggingCorrelation.UserMessage); ... Detail = loggingCorrelation.UserMessage

strengths.subject: Security
strengths.title: Unhandled and repository-level exceptions are logged internally with full exception detail and a correlation ID before a sanitized message reaches the client

evidence.excerpt: this.Logger.LogError(exInner, "Error occurred in {ClassName}.{MethodName}. CorrelationId: {CorrelationId}", nameof(TestingRepository), nameof(ResetTestingAsync), loggingCorrelation.CorrelationId); throw new UserException(loggingCorrelation.UserMessage);

strengths.subject: Security
strengths.title: DataSourceConfiguration.ToString() explicitly redacts the Password field before any diagnostic string conversion

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: Request logging (Serilog UseSerilogRequestLogging) and repository logging use parameterized message templates (e.g. {RequestPath}, {CorrelationId}), not string-concatenated user input; no raw user input written to logs was found in the files in scope.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: The Password value committed in both appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json is the literal placeholder string "<DevUser password>", not a functional credential; no other hardcoded API keys, tokens or connection strings were found in the files in scope.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: Credential fields (Password, UserName) are part of the checked-in appsettings*.json schema and flow directly into a plaintext connection string; although a UserSecretsId is declared, nothing in the reviewed files enforces sourcing the real value from user-secrets/environment/Key Vault rather than editing the committed file.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: Review prioritized the exception-handling middleware, logging config/extensions, secrets-bearing appsettings files and the repository that builds DB connection strings, per the Secure Code Review Cheat Sheet method.

notes: Read a small set of closely related files beyond the given scope (UserException.cs, ApplicationConfiguration.cs, DataSourceConfiguration.cs, ApiExtensions.cs, Program.cs, PilotUtilityApi.Web.csproj, .gitignore, logs/) to confirm how errors/secrets are handled end-to-end and to verify logs/ is gitignored (it is, so committed log-leakage was ruled out). Corrected SEC-OP-06's severityIfFailed to Warning (matching the finding's assigned severity) — the subagent's raw output stated Error for severityIfFailed while assigning the finding itself Warning severity given the value is a placeholder, not a live credential; Warning is used consistently for scoring.
